headline: AL leader Hanif sentenced to death for crimes against humanity in Kushtia
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death and three others to imprisonment until death for the killing of six people during the July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Awami League Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death for crimes against humanity involving the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July Uprising.

Three other accused—former Kushtia district council chairman Sadar Uddin Khan, District General Secretary Azgar Ali, and former Sadar Upazila council chairman Ataur Rahman Ata—were sentenced to imprisonment until death.
The tribunal, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, found the convicts guilty on multiple counts, including direct orders to kill students and members of the public.
The verdict also includes the confiscation of half of the convicts' immovable property, with proceeds to be given as compensation to the victims through the July Foundation or another statutory body.
The prosecution brought charges of 'command responsibility', alleging the convicts endorsed statements that party activists were sufficient to 'deal' with protesters.
A total of 19 witnesses, including the investigating officer, testified during the trial, which began on November 2 last year.
caption:
A top Awami League leader has been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Awami League Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death for crimes against humanity involving the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July Uprising.

Three other accused—former Kushtia district council chairman Sadar Uddin Khan, District General Secretary Azgar Ali, and former Sadar Upazila council chairman Ataur Rahman Ata—were sentenced to imprisonment until death.

The tribunal, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, found the convicts guilty on multiple counts, including direct orders to kill students and members of the public.

The verdict also includes the confiscation of half of the convicts' immovable property, with proceeds to be given as compensation to the victims through the July Foundation or another statutory body.

The prosecution brought charges of 'command responsibility', alleging the convicts endorsed statements that party activists were sufficient to 'deal' with protesters.

A total of 19 witnesses, including the investigating officer, testified during the trial, which began on November 2 last year.

headline_marked: Rail link cut: [[Neelsagar Express derails in Tangail]], suspending Dhaka-north services
headline: Rail link cut: Neelsagar Express derails in Tangail, suspending Dhaka-north services
summary: A carriage of the train derailed near Mahera Railway Station, damaging a track point and leaving multiple trains stranded.
details: Train services between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh have been suspended after a carriage of the Neelsagar Express derailed near Mahera Railway Station in Mirzapur, Tangail, this morning.
The incident occurred around 9:30am, leaving several trains stranded at different stations and causing significant hardship for passengers.
The Neelsagar Express, which departed from Dhaka for Chilahati, derailed when the wheels of one of its rear carriages veered off the tracks.
According to Mahera Railway Station master Sohel Rana, the derailment damaged a track point, which disrupted rail traffic in the region.
Recovery work was already under way by 11:00am to restore the rail link and resume services.
caption:
Rail links between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh are cut after the Neelsagar Express derailed in Tangail.

Train services between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh have been suspended after a carriage of the Neelsagar Express derailed near Mahera Railway Station in Mirzapur, Tangail, this morning.

The incident occurred around 9:30am, leaving several trains stranded at different stations and causing significant hardship for passengers.

The Neelsagar Express, which departed from Dhaka for Chilahati, derailed when the wheels of one of its rear carriages veered off the tracks.

According to Mahera Railway Station master Sohel Rana, the derailment damaged a track point, which disrupted rail traffic in the region.

Recovery work was already under way by 11:00am to restore the rail link and resume services.
